test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-II Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2025)
subject: general
question: A shopkeeper fixes the marked price of an item 90% above its cost price. What percentage of discount on marked price should be allowed to gain 71%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100.

Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 90% = 190

Selling Price (SP) for 71% profit = 100 + 71% = 171

Discount = MP − SP = 190 − 171 = 19

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (19 ÷ 190) × 100 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mark-up Percentage = 90% above CP

Profit Percentage = 71%

**Formula Used:**

Ratio of CP to MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%)

 
 
 
 
• CP = 100 SP = 171 MP = 190 
 +90% Markup 
 +71% Profit 
 −d% Discount 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let CP be 100

⇒ MP = 100 + 90 = 190

⇒ Using the formula: CP ÷ MP = (100 − D) ÷ (100 + P)

⇒ 100 ÷ 190 = (100 − D) ÷ (100 + 71)

⇒ 10 ÷ 19 = (100 − D) ÷ 171

⇒ 100 − D = (171 × 10) ÷ 19

⇒ 100 − D = 9 × 10

⇒ 100 − D = 90

⇒ D = 100 − 90 = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Relation Between CP and MP

The most efficient way to link Cost Price and Marked Price is using the ratio formula: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Successive Discounts

When two consecutive discounts x% and y% are given on MP, the single equivalent discount = [x + y − (xy ÷ 100)]%.

Mark-up Percentage

It indicates how much more the Marked Price is compared to the Cost Price. Formula: Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.
